overview.title: Company overview
overview.lede: India's largest private-sector bank by balance sheet (₹43.65 lakh cr) and market cap (₹11.20 lakh cr) — a universal-banking franchise reshaped by the July-2023 reverse merger with parent HDFC Ltd, which folded the country's largest mortgage book into Retail.

mix_gap.label: NOT SEPARATELY DISCLOSED
mix_gap.text: A universal bank's segment revenue split (Retail / Wholesale / Treasury) is not carried on the Tickertape feed this run, so it is a labelled gap rather than a fabricated treemap. The franchise table at right is what the annual report does disclose.

overview.moat: The moat is scale plus distribution — the largest private-bank branch network, the deepest CASA franchise, and cross-sell into a merged home-loan base — not a licence-scarcity moat, since ICICI, Axis and Kotak compete directly. The live question is the post-merger ROE rebuild (13.26% now vs a 16–17% pre-merger best), which is the entire debate.

sector_story.title: Does the industry have a future?
sector_story.lede: Yes, structurally: credit is still small relative to the economy and private banks keep taking share from state-owned ones. The near-term story is weaker, because deposit growth is lagging loan growth across the system.

cards.label: SYSTEM CREDIT
cards.sub: FY26 · RBI data via AR MD&A

drivers.text: Credit penetration is low by emerging-market standards, so loan growth can outrun nominal GDP for years.
Private banks keep gaining share from state-owned banks on deposits and retail loans.
Digital payments rails lower the cost of acquiring deposits.

risks.text: Deposits are growing slower than loans across the system, squeezing margins.
Unsecured retail stress has risen and regulators have raised risk weights.

policy.text: Higher risk weights on unsecured consumer credit and loans to NBFCs.
Revised liquidity coverage norms for retail deposits phased in.

sector_story.read: The industry tailwind is real and long; it does not rescue a bank whose own deposit franchise is lagging, which is this one's problem.

glance.title: The six lenses
glance.lede: Four lenses lean negative or neutral; the balance sheet is the one clear strength. The call is carried by financials — NIM breaking its own floor — corroborated by news and sector, with valuation and technicals in genuine, unresolved tension.

lenses.name: SECTOR
lenses.read: Private banks are Leading vs Nifty (credit growth a 2-year high, system GNPA a multi-decadal low), but HDFCBANK is the one laggard within the sector on both 1M and 3M relative strength.

lenses.name: TECHNICAL
lenses.read: Price is pinned almost exactly on the ₹727 floor for two straight weekly closes — a genuine decision point, not a confirmed breakdown — but a fresh lower low and a bearish MA stack lean bearish.

lenses.name: FINANCIALS
lenses.read: Fortress capital (CRAR 19.7%, improving GNPA/NNPA) sits alongside NIM compression (3.48%→3.34%→3.26%) and two years of EPS flattered ~9–10% by one-off stake-sale gains.

lenses.name: MANAGEMENT
lenses.read: Economically clean — trivial pay, arm's-length RPTs, no promoter overhang — but downgraded from a clean PASS to FLAG on live, CEO-concentrated regulatory/legal threads unresolved as of today.

lenses.name: VALUATION
lenses.read: 16–24% cheap to peers on P/E and P/B, but the reverse-ROE check shows CMP still implies ~18–20% sustained ROE — above even the pre-merger 16–17% best, against a current 13.26%.

lenses.name: NEWS
lenses.read: NIM breaching its own floor lands in the same window as a CEO-succession/governance scandal drawing a US securities class action, only partly offset by a clean investment-grade dollar-bond raise.

story.title: How it started, and how it got here
story.lede: A single-product lender founded by a parent institution grew into a universal bank through two acquisitions and one reverse merger. Each step widened the franchise; the last one also diluted returns, which is the debate today.
narrative: The bank was set up by its parent as one of the first private banks licensed after liberalisation, with a mandate to serve the parent's corporate relationships and a small retail book.

Growth came in three steps: organic branch expansion through the 2000s, two bank acquisitions that brought retail deposits, and a reverse merger with the parent that folded a large mortgage book onto the balance sheet.

timeline.what: Incorporated with an in-principle banking licence.
Begins operations; lists on the exchanges.
First acquisition: a smaller private bank, adding branches and deposits.
Second acquisition doubles the branch network.
Reverse merger with the parent; mortgage book and the parent's shareholders come across.
Integration year: deposits rebuilt, loan-to-deposit ratio brought back under 95%.

scorecard.title: The due-diligence scorecard
scorecard.lede: Two of seven checks pass on the literal checklist — but four of the flags are the checklist meeting a bank, where ROCE, operating margin and CFO-vs-EBITDA are not meaningful; the real defects are NIM compression and one-off-flattered earnings.
scorecard.workings: Other Income carried a large one-off subsidiary stake-sale gain in both of the last two years — ₹9,179 Cr (HDB Financial, FY26) and ₹7,341 Cr (Credila, FY25). Stripping the post-tax FY26 gain at the 21.54% effective rate cuts clean EPS to ~₹43.9 against a reported ₹48.62 — a 9.7% haircut, squarely in the FLAG band, and a recurring pattern, not a one-off. Source: annual report FY26 MD&A p.259, p.215.
scorecard.footer: Ratios & statements: Tickertape + annual report FY26 MD&A · a bank's ROCE / operating margin / CFO-vs-EBITDA are marked not-meaningful, not scored PASS · NIM & GNPA from MD&A

record.title: The record, and what it isn't
record.lede: Headline revenue compounded ~26% over five years — but that is merger arithmetic, not organic momentum: assets nearly doubled FY23→FY24 on the HDFC Ltd absorption, while per-share earnings grew only ~11.3% as the merger diluted the share count ~40%.

dcf.title: What the business is worth
dcf.lede: ₹407.63 a share on a partial-ROE-recovery story at a 13.95% cost of equity — a −43.9% margin of safety. This is a bank, so the DCF is graded low confidence by construction; the relative read leads.
dcf.build_title: Where the value comes from · ₹ per share (FCFE-equivalent)
dcf.inputs_label: INPUTS · THE STORY BEHIND THE NUMBER
dcf.inputs: A bank's FCFF is ill-defined (capex is a rounding error next to net income), so this is the standard Damodaran FCFE-equivalent adaptation: net income as the base, marginal ROE as the sales-to-capital lever. Net-income growth 9%→13%→6.5% terminal; marginal ROE recovers from 13.26% to a partial 14.5% — barely above the 13.95% cost of equity, so growth is only weakly value-accretive. That thin excess return is the central finding.

sensitivity.title: Sensitivity · fair value ₹, growth × steady-state margin

dcf.reverse: The reverse DCF is sharper: ₹726.95 needs a ~28.6% 10-year net-income CAGR, or a sustained ~18–20% ROE — both above the pre-merger 16–17% ceiling. Even a +4% growth shift only reaches ₹461, ~37% below the price.

debate.lede: Round 2 was real engagement: the bull answered the growth-durability axis with fresh Q1FY27 arithmetic; the bear answered the valuation axis by re-reading the bull's own cited source. The bear won the price question; the bull won the earnings-level question.

bull.thesis: A fortress balance sheet at a real, only-partly-explained discount to peers — and earnings that are still growing in level terms right through the NIM miss.
claims: 24% headline P/E discount to peers, 16% even on clean one-off-adjusted EPS, 16% on P/B — inside an already-cheap large-cap tier.
CRAR 19.7%, borrowings-only D/E down 1.21×→0.53× in three years, GNPA/NNPA improving, PCR raised to 210%.
Q1FY27 NII +6.7% and PAT +5% YoY in the very quarter NIM hit its record low — loan growth is offsetting margin compression at the earnings level.
bull.conceded: That the clean-EPS-adjusted peer discount narrows from 24% to ~16%, and that the CD-ratio normalisation reversed in Q1FY27 — honest concessions, not papered over.

bear.thesis: Ten years of flat pre-merger ROE says the price is a full-recovery bet not yet delivered — 82× the recovery, not the record. NIM has broken its own floor.
claims: NIM 3.48%→3.34%→3.26% breached the prior thesis's own invalidation trigger — corroborated by financials, news and sector.
The reverse DCF needs a ~28.6% net-income CAGR, or a sustained ~18–20% ROE — above the pre-merger 16–17% best, vs 13.26% now.
Two years of one-off subsidiary stake-sale gains flattered EPS ~9–10%; the DCF's own 3.38% stress case has already been breached to 3.26%.
bear.conceded: That governance is economically clean and the balance sheet carries no hidden leverage — the bear's case is entirely about price and ROE-recovery, not quality.

debate.decided: Both sides are right about different questions. The load-bearing fact kept was the NIM-trigger breach, weighted because three independent legs corroborate it; the bear's round-2 textual correction of the DCF reconciliation held up on the PM's own re-check. The bull's NII/PAT-still-growing point is the strongest surviving losing argument and is kept as dissent. AVOID, medium conviction — no position to exit, and a concentrated October event-risk window worth waiting through. Weakest input: the Q1FY27 NIM print.

invalidation.title: What would change the call
invalidation.lede: Four conditions, each machine-checkable and re-tested every run. Two are price levels, two are business facts. The single one that decides it is the Q2FY27 NIM print.

conditions.condition: Weekly close reclaims and holds above ₹748–750
conditions.why: Former support turned resistance. A reclaim negates the bearish structure and, with a NIM stabilise, rehabilitates the bull case.

conditions.condition: Q2FY27 NIM stabilises back above 3.26% (no fresh one-off)
conditions.why: The load-bearing fact. A clean stabilisation weakens the 'growth durability broken' framing materially.

conditions.condition: A third weekly close decisively below ₹715
conditions.why: Confirms the technical breakdown the two pinned closes have so far left undecided.

conditions.condition: A disclosed RBI/board resolution against the CEO
conditions.why: Any adjudicated outcome on the MSRDC / Lilavati threads re-opens the integrity gate immediately.

invalidation.review: Q2 FY27 results (~19 Oct 2026) and the CEO third-term/RBI decision — both land in the same month. Re-run sooner if a weekly close resolves the ₹715/₹748 ambiguity first.
